title: Canonical matched-empty trial table (omission.jnwb_ext.matched_empty) -- frozen after independent verification
notes: build_matched_empty_table(session, slots=(2,3,4)) produces the ONE canonical omission-vs-ordinary-empty-time trial table shared by SPK/LFP/MUAe -- five comparator types: omission, local_pre_omission_delay, post_omission_delay, trial_delay_mean (all is_empty=True except omission), stimulus_present_control (is_empty=False, real-stimulus, unpaired trial pool).

BUG (found 2026-08-27, during initial build, before any independent verification): detect_trial_cycles was called on the long-form comparator-expanded table directly, which repeats each physical omission trial's p1_onset_s across 4 rows and interleaves separately-onset control trials. This corrupted the gap-threshold cycle-clustering algorithm: 598 spurious 'cycles' from ~340-596 actual physical trials on a real-session smoke test (sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec) -- logically backwards, since cycles should group trials into far fewer blocks, not more.

FIX v1 (2026-08-27): deduplicate to one row per distinct p1_onset_s AFTER building the full expanded table, compute cycle_id once on that deduplicated frame, left-merge cycle_id back onto every comparator row. Verified: cycle count dropped from 598 to 3 (596 unique physical trials), 0 NaN cycle_id, every row sharing a trial's onset shares one cycle_id. This fix is what the first independent verifier (agent a41ff7d33886a94ad) reviewed and CONFIRMED.

FIX v2 (2026-08-27, post-verification, Hamm's explicit matched-empty gate item 5): refactored to a genuine two-pass structure -- PASS 1 builds one row per distinct physical trial (omission_trial or control_trial, no comparator-type expansion) and assigns cycle_id once over the deduplicated whole-session onset union; PASS 2 expands each physical trial into its comparator-type rows, attaching the already-known cycle_id. This makes 'cycle assignment happens before comparator expansion' a literal code-order fact, not merely an emergent safety property of the merge -- v1 had the correct SAFETY property (detect_trial_cycles never touched duplicated rows) but the literal ORDER was expansion-then-cycle-then-merge-back, not cycle-then-expansion. v2 output is row-for-row identical to v1 on the real corpus (same 4/4 regression tests pass unchanged; a 5th test was added pinning the new invariant).

Gate item 4 (verify physical trial IDs unique before cycle detection): verified empirically against sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec -- 0 duplicate p1_onset_s values within any single condition's om_epochs/ctrl_epochs pool, and 0 duplicate onset values globally across all conditions combined. This is an invariant of trial start_time, not merely assumed; see test_physical_trial_onsets_unique_before_cycle_dedup.

One real behavior surfaced while adding that test (not a defect): a control trial's onset MAY appear more than once in the PASS-1 pool, because the same physical control trial can legitimately be resampled as the matched 'stimulus_present_control' for multiple distinct omission events within one family (independent per-(condition,slot) draws against the same shared control-condition trial pool). Omission trials never repeat (exactly 1 pool row -> exactly 4 comparator rows each). Both cases still resolve to exactly one cycle_id per physical trial via the onset->cycle dict built in PASS 1.

Independent verification (agent a41ff7d33886a94ad, fresh context, live-data cross-checks against sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec): CONFIRMED. _preceding_identity's slot-2 indexing verified by hand against 5 live conditions and confirmed structurally immune to the documented omission_identity.py p4 A/B dict-key swap (reads the raw condition string, never touches that dict). All four empty-comparator windows verified genuinely disjoint from the omission slot (0 overlaps on live data). stimulus_present_control verified to draw from a genuinely separate trial pool (0 onset overlap with the omission-trial pool). Two non-blocking caveats recorded: (a) trial_index is unique only within (condition, omission_slot), not globally -- a downstream join on trial_index alone would silently pair unrelated physical trials; (b) the docstring's claimed trial_index=-1 sentinel for unpaired control rows is never actually emitted by any code path (unmatched conditions simply omit the row) -- doc/implementation mismatch, not a scientific defect.

issues.description: trial_index is only unique within (condition, omission_slot). Any downstream consumer must join/group on the full (condition, omission_slot, trial_index) composite key, never trial_index alone.
issues.action: flag in matched_empty.py docstring before P4/Gate-1 code reuses this table; not fixed in data, by design (composite key already present and correct).

issues.description: Docstring historically claimed trial_index=-1 for unpaired control rows; no code path sets it. Unmatched control conditions simply produce zero stimulus_present_control rows for that (condition,slot).

verification.scope: matched_empty.py v1 (pre two-pass refactor) against unit_classification.py and sequence_layout.py, live-checked on sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec.nwb

matched_empty.py v2 (two-pass refactor): literal PASS1-before-PASS2 ordering, no duplicated onset ever reaches detect_trial_cycles, float dict-key safety for the onset->cycle lookup, live run against sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec.nwb (1700 rows, cycle_id nunique=2 vs 591-596 physical trials, 0 cycle_id inconsistencies including for reused control onsets), and a precise reconstructed-v1-vs-actual-v2 diff (0 mismatches across all 1700 rows).
verification.issue_found: rng_local = np.random.default_rng(abs(hash((cond, slot))) % (2**31)) used Python's built-in hash() on a (str,int) tuple, which is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED randomized by default unless pinned) -- so which control trial gets matched to which omission event was NOT reproducible across separate script invocations on identical data (empirically confirmed: 3 bare invocations gave 591/594/596 differing unique physical trial counts for the same NWB file). This did not affect the ordering/cycle-assignment correctness verified above (checked within one process), but broke the 'same input -> same output table' reproducibility guarantee any downstream analysis built on this table would need.
verification.fix: replaced hash((cond,slot)) with zlib.crc32(f'{cond}_{slot}'.encode()) (2026-08-27). Verified: 3 separate bare-process invocations against sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec.nwb now give identical n_rows (1700), identical n_unique_onsets (597), and identical control-onset checksum (sum of all control p1_onset_s values, matched to 6 decimal places) across all 3 runs. Full regression suite (19/19, test_matched_empty.py + test_causal_validation.py) re-passed after the fix.
